note: Market sentiment & global flows for the overview. Fear&Greed is fetched LIVE in-browser (CNN equity index via proxy + crypto via alternative.me) with the baked value as fallback; breadth & regional flows are researched and baked (no free real-time API) and refreshed daily by the scheduled intel agent.

components.name: Market Momentum
components.reading: S&P 500 vs its 125-day moving average. The index closed June 25 at ~7,357, back above its rising 125-day average after recovering from the June 23 semiconductor rout — Micron's blowout fiscal-Q3 results (SanDisk +14.7%, Micron +12% on June 25) drove a memory/AI-led rebound. Momentum has firmed back to neutral.

components.name: Stock Price Strength
components.reading: Net 52-week highs vs lows on the NYSE. Small-cap leadership broadened the tape — the Russell 2000 crossed 3,000 for the first time ever on June 22 and the small-cap A-D line printed a new all-time high — lifting net new highs back toward neutral after the chip wobble.

components.name: Stock Price Breadth
components.reading: McClellan Volume Summation (advancing vs declining volume). Breadth is broadening: NYSE advancers beat decliners on June 25 (~1,225 vs ~983) and the Summation Index is grinding higher, with participation widening beyond mega-cap tech.

components.name: Put/Call Options
components.reading: 5-day put/call ratio. Despite the rebound, options buyers stayed defensive into a hawkish Fed and a hot core-PCE print, keeping the 5-day ratio tilted toward puts.

components.name: Market Volatility
components.reading: VIX vs its 50-day moving average. The VIX closed June 25 at 18.63 — mid-range and roughly near its 50-day average, well off the early-June war-scare highs and not at a fear extreme.

components.name: Safe Haven Demand
components.reading: 20-day stock vs Treasury bond return spread. Treasuries stayed bid as the 10-year fell to ~4.4% (a 6-week low on the Iran de-escalation), so bonds have kept pace with stocks over the trailing window — a still-defensive read.

components.name: Junk Bond Demand
components.reading: Yield spread between junk bonds and investment-grade. HY OAS remains historically tight (~265-285bp), but BofA flagged HY/EM bond-fund outflows and put-heavy HY hedging, so demand for risky credit is cooling at the margin.

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 200-day MA
metrics.value: ~61.8% (Barchart $S5TH live June 25, off a 1-month high of 64.1 and well up from the June 2 low of 53.1) — a constructive, above-half reading

metrics.label: % of S&P 500 stocks above 50-day MA
metrics.value: ~58% (Barchart $S5FI; recovered from sub-50% early-June lows and now back above its own 50-day MA, though shy of the 60%+ highs)

metrics.label: NYSE advancers vs decliners (latest session)
metrics.value: Advancers led on June 25 (~1,225 vs ~983), with small-caps (Russell 2000 +0.4%) outperforming — a healthier internal than the June 23 down-session (approximate, $ADRN)

metrics.label: 52-week New Highs minus New Lows (NYSE)
metrics.value: Recovered toward positive as the rebound broadened and small-caps led; precise live counts not extractable from JS-rendered tables (approximate)

metrics.label: NYSE McClellan Oscillator / Summation Index
metrics.value: The Summation Index has turned higher and breadth indicators have held above the 50% threshold since mid-May, signaling broadening participation (mcoscillator.com); the June 23 chip rout did not durably reverse the improvement (approximate; exact daily NYMO not published in accessible sources)

metrics.label: Cumulative NYSE Advance-Decline line trend
metrics.value: Rising and confirming — the broad A-D line is trending up and the small-cap A-D line made a new all-time high, a notably healthier picture than the narrow tape of earlier in June (approximate trend read, not a single figure)

metrics.label: % of 11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA
metrics.value: Approximate ~73% (roughly 8 of 11 sector ETFs) as leadership broadened beyond Technology into Financials, Industrials and Health Care; the late-June rebound lifted most sectors back above trend (inferred from index-level breadth and sector leadership)

breadth.note: Breadth has broadened and improved through late June: after the June 23 semiconductor-led drawdown, Micron's blowout earnings (June 25) sparked a memory/AI-led rebound, the Russell 2000 hit a record 3,000 with the small-cap A-D line at an all-time high, and ~62% of the S&P now sits above its 200-DMA with advancers beating decliners and leadership rotating out of the mega-cap concentration that had dominated the tape. This is a healthier, less narrow internal than the prior reading — the open question is whether a hot core-PCE print (3.4%) and a hawkish, hike-biased Fed cap the broadening.

flows.period: EPFR 'Flow Show' detail covers the week to June 7 (published June 24); ICI mutual-fund/ETF data covers the week ended June 17 (reported June 24). Weekly and lagged — no fresher fully-itemized week had printed by June 26.
flows.narrative: A powerful rotation INTO US assets. BofA/EPFR's June 24 'Global Navigator: Rotating towards the US' showed all-equity funds taking a record-tier ~$126.4B (US equity funds a record), bond funds +$19.7B and money-market funds +$25.1B, with tech/semiconductor funds a standout (the ~$21.5B weekly tech allocation). Corroborating ICI data for the week ended June 17 showed +$55.75B into equity funds (domestic +$49.6B), +$16.46B into bonds and a $1.31B outflow from commodity/gold funds. The clear laggards: Latin America bled for a fifth straight week and crypto funds shed roughly $6.6B over five weeks. The flows remain weekly and lagged, and BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator sits at ~8.8 — extending a multi-week contrarian 'sell' signal even as the late-June tape rebounded.

regions.note: EPFR flagged a record US-equity-fund week and >$170B into US-mandated equity+bond+MMF assets combined — the dominant rotation was decisively toward the US.
ICI world/international equity funds drew $6.15B; within EPFR's Europe bucket only EMEA equity funds showed clean inflows (Poland a 4th straight week).
EM was EMEA-led on the inflow side, but Latin America equity funds bled for a fifth straight week (~3.5% of asset base), keeping aggregate EM ex-EMEA soft.
No clean weekly figure broken out; China sits within the soft EM ex-EMEA complex, outflow-leaning and unconfirmed.
Japan was not individually itemized in the public EPFR/ICI excerpts this week; flow direction unconfirmed.
Money-market funds kept absorbing large inflows alongside the equity surge — a defensive undertone despite the risk-on equity headline, consistent with the ~8.8 Bull & Bear 'sell' read.
Global bond funds extended their multi-week inflow streak (taxable +$13.43B, muni +$3.03B in ICI); demand skewed to IG/short-duration over HY in a higher-for-longer backdrop.
Commodity/gold funds bled $1.31B (a smaller outflow than the prior week's -$2.27B) as gold slid further to ~$4,040 on firm real yields and a hawkish Fed.

movements.note: The defining rotation — a record US-equity-fund week plus heavy US bond and money-market inflows as allocators concentrated into the US.
Tech/semis remained the single most-favored sector despite the June 23 chip wobble; Micron's June 25 beat then validated the AI-memory bid.
Latin America extended a fifth weekly outflow (~3.5% of base) as a hawkish Fed and firm dollar kept the rotation toward the US and select EMEA.
Persistent bleed from gold and digital-asset funds (crypto F&G hit Extreme Fear at 13) as firm real yields and the unwound war premium sapped the safe-haven/alt bid.
